newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage-backed market shrugs off economic data.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage-backed market shrugs off economic data.

text.p: A flurry of economic data that included increases in June housing starts and the July Philadelphia Federal Reserve business index had little immediate effect on mortgage-backed securities (MBS), said market participants.
One investor said he would have expected some reaction in U.S. Treasuries to the Philadelpia Fed index rise to 28.1 in July from June's 25.2. Treasuries also ended little changed.
Remarks by a Fed economist may have tempered any fears of inflation; the Fed economist contended that it is too early to say the rise in the index suggested an industry rebound.

Also, a rise in the Mortgage Bankers Association refinancing index seemed to be digested by MBS without event. The seasonally adjusted 22.7 percent rise in the week ended July 11 was expected, given the recent interest rate decline, participants said.
Meanwhile, market players said they saw some down-in-coupon activity to dodge prepayment risk and there was movement into Treasuries from mortgage-backeds.
"We did see some flows out of 7.5 percent and 8.0 percent coupons," said one market participant.

Among active MBS issues, Government National Mortgage Association 30-year 7.5-percent coupons were off 1/32 at 101 12/32. Comparable Federal National Mortgage Association 7.5-percent coupons were up 1/32 at 101 9/32, while comparable Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp 7.5-percent coupons were off 2/32 at 101 13/32.
A New York pass-through trader said he saw "large sales" of 8.0 percent coupons in the last couple of sessions.

Mortgages will take cues from Treasuries, the other trader noted. If Treasury prices rally, mortgages "will suffer hard and if rates back up or remain steady, then mortgages will hang in there," the New York trader said.
But, the pass-through trader noted that while there has been a great deal of talk about prepayment fears, there has not been a wholesale selloff of mortgage securities.
"Mortgages have shortened pretty dramatically and have reached a critical zone of nervousness based on dollar prices and the negative convexity of mortgages," the pass-through trader contended.

Trenton Fletcher, who manages a $1 billion mortgage-backed portfolio for Key Asset Management, said that "the key to outperformance over the next six months will be staying on top of technical moves rather than large strategic shifts."

One investor who actually moved up in coupon contended that the economy "seems far too strong to justify further decreases in rates." He added that he does not expect the 10-year Treasury note to linger below 6.0 percent for a long period if it does dip below that level.
Ten-year Treasury notes were priced to yield 6.19 percent late Thursday.
